verdicts.explanation: The evidence span from the community forum (eval:18373201ffdd59b847ca27a045ee4bcb2d1470a26f2d55d77d08d851f4092b1f:0) shows a user (SoWeVibinNow) describing their iPhone 14 Pro and asking about battery capacity concerns, specifically stating 'I got my iPhone 14 Pro just a few days back and I really don't want to ruin the capacity to reach 90 % in not even a year.' This directly supports the claim that one user describes their iPhone 14 Pro battery capacity concerns.

The evidence spans from two community forum posts directly support the claim. Span eval:cb05ea5a2c752ea6e63bfa74c6b208a32ed044eb7389c923b817ef1949d83e06:0 shows a user (Claymore6) describing their iPhone 11 Pro battery capacity dropping from 85% to 79% after warranty expiration, detailing degraded battery. Span eval:116bad1da49c8429bb597ff3f83e0a974728c99bc795a376bd962f41734574a4:0 shows a user (NoSoulRequired) describing a third-party battery replacement for an iPhone 11 that resulted in 'unknown part' error and loss of battery health features, detailing third-party replacement issues.

All evidence spans in the packet discuss iPhone battery health, charging practices, and battery replacement issues. None of the spans mention the Flare 2 or Ortizan 40W speakers, nor do they discuss battery life or charging behavior of these specific products. The discussions are entirely about iPhone batteries, confirming the claim that these discussions are irrelevant to the battery life or charging behavior of the Flare 2 or Ortizan 40W.
